pi_tau_policy.pi_form: R_pi(z) = (2z - 1) * pi^{-2z} * zeta(2z) = pi^{-z} * xi(2z) / Gamma(z + 1)
pi_tau_policy.tau_first_simplification: tau^{-2m} zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} / (2*(2m)!) strips out the artificial 2^{2m} = 4^m factor present in pi^{-2m} zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1} 2^{2m-1} B_{2m} / (2m)!
pi_tau_policy.normalization_dependent_factors: Gauge power c^z (4^z for pi vs 1 for tau), sample factor c^m (4^m), moment factor c^{m+1} (4^{m+1}), Hankel factor c^{n^2} (4^{n^2}), 2-adic denominator valuation shift -2n, saddle constants kappa(c) = (3/2^{5/3}) c^{1/3}
pi_tau_policy.normalization_invariant_factors: Zero divisor {z in C : R_c(z) = 0}, odd-prime p-adic valuations v_p(a_m) for p >= 3, Newton polynomial degree n, stretched-exponential exponent n^{1/3}, Newton denominator leading order n log n, Hankel denominator leading order 2 n^2 log n

R_pi.pi_form: R_pi(z) = (2z - 1) * pi^{-2z} * zeta(2z) = pi^{-z} * xi(2z) / Gamma(z + 1)
R_pi.tau_first_simplification: Obtained from primitive R_tau(z) by multiplying by the nowhere-zero gauge 4^z
R_pi.normalization_dependent_factors: 4^z = exp(z log 4), value at z = 1/2 is R_pi(1/2) = 1/pi = 2/tau
R_pi.normalization_invariant_factors: Entire status on C, simple pole cancellation at z = 1/2, zeros at z = rho/2 and z = -m (m >= 1)

R_tau.tau_first_simplification: Exposes the pure Bernoulli/factorial rational core a_m^{(tau)} = (-1)^{m+1} (2m-1) B_{2m} / (2*(2m)!) at nonnegative integers m without any dyadic 2^{2m} numerator multiplier
R_tau.normalization_dependent_factors: Gauge c = 1, value at z = 1/2 is R_tau(1/2) = 1/(2*tau) = 1/(4*pi)
R_tau.normalization_invariant_factors: Entire status on C, simple pole cancellation at z = 1/2, zeros at z = rho/2 and z = -m (m >= 1)

zero_divisor_equivalence.equivalence_statement: For all z in C, R_pi(z) = 0 <=> R_tau(z) = 0 <=> R_c(z) = 0 (for any c > 0)
zero_divisor_equivalence.proof: 4^z = exp(z log 4) != 0 and c^z = exp(z log c) != 0 on all of C

tau_even_zeta_rational_core.tau_first_simplification: Because Euler's formula is zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} (2*pi)^{2m} / (2*(2m)!) = (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} tau^{2m} / (2*(2m)!), dividing by tau^{2m} leaves the pure rational core (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} / (2*(2m)!) in Q_{>0}.

sample_scaling.identity: a_m^{(pi)} = 4^m * a_m^{(tau)} and a_m^{(c)} = c^m * a_m^{(tau)}

rational_gauge_family.definition: R_c(z) := c^z * R_tau(z) = (2z - 1) * c^z * tau^{-2z} * zeta(2z) = (2*tau/c)^{-z} * xi(2z) / Gamma(z + 1)

gauge_zero_invariance.statement: For every c in Q_{>0} and every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s), R_c(rho / 2) = 0
gauge_zero_invariance.analytic_vs_arithmetic_firewall: Changing c in Q_{>0} leaves the complex analytic zero divisor {z : R_c(z) = 0} strictly invariant, while rescaling the arithmetic interpolation samples by a_m^{(c)} = c^m a_m^{(tau)}.

A_pi.formula: A_pi(t) = sum_{m>=0} a_m^{(pi)} t^m = t / (2 * sin^2(sqrt(t)))

A_tau.formula: A_tau(t) = sum_{m>=0} a_m^{(tau)} t^m = t / (8 * sin^2(sqrt(t) / 2))
A_tau.nearest_pole: t = tau^2 = 4 * pi^2 (double pole where sqrt(t)/2 = pi)

A_c.formula: A_c(t) = A_tau(c * t) = (c * t) / (8 * sin^2(sqrt(c * t) / 2))

C_pi.formula: C_pi(w) = sum_{n>=0} (Delta^n a_0^{(pi)}) w^n = w / (2 * (1 + w)^2 * sin^2(sqrt(w / (1 + w))))

C_c.singular_behavior_near_w_eq_neg1: For s = 1 + w in C \ (-infty, 0] with principal branch sqrt(s), w / (1 + w) = -(1 - s)/s, so (1/2)*sqrt(c*w/(1+w)) = (i/2)*sqrt(c*(1-s)/s), sin^2((1/2)*sqrt(c*w/(1+w))) = -sinh^2((1/2)*sqrt(c*(1-s)/s)) ~ -(1/4)*exp(sqrt(c)/sqrt(s))*(1 - (1/2)*sqrt(c*s)), giving C_c(-1 + s) = (c * (1 - s) / (2 * s^2)) * exp(-sqrt(c)/sqrt(s)) * (1 - (1/2)*sqrt(c*s) + O(s))^{-1} ~ (c / (2 * s^2)) * exp(-sqrt(c) / sqrt(s)).
C_c.branch_and_sector_conventions: Principal square root sqrt(s) = |s|^{1/2} exp(i arg(s)/2) on arg(s) in (-pi, pi); Re(1/sqrt(s)) > 0 across the entire cut plane |arg(s)| < pi, with conjugate saddles at arg(s) = +- 2*pi/3 where 1/sqrt(s) = |s|^{-1/2} exp(-+ i*pi/3) = |s|^{-1/2} * (1/2 -+ i*sqrt(3)/2) still has positive real part +1/2 |s|^{-1/2}.

saddle_points.why_no_pi_factor_in_saddles: Because a_m^{(pi)} = (2m-1) pi^{-2m} zeta(2m) already normalizes out pi^{-2m}, the OGF A_pi(t) = t / (2 sin^2(sqrt(t))) has dimensionless Taylor variable t, so C_pi(-1+s) ~ (2/s^2) exp(-2/sqrt(s)) contains NO factor of pi in its exponential argument.

delta_n_a0_full_asymptotic.formula: Delta^n a_0^{(c)} = (-1)^{n+1} * K(c) * n^{mu} * exp(-kappa(c) * n^{1/3}) * [cos(omega(c) * n^{1/3} + phi(c)) + O(n^{-eta})]
delta_n_a0_full_asymptotic.K_c_formula: K(c) = 2 * sqrt(c) / sqrt(3 * pi)  (K(4) = 4 / sqrt(3*pi), K(1) = 2 / sqrt(3*pi))

newton_identity_proof.gauge_parameter_range: 0 < c < tau^2 = 4*pi^2 (includes c = 1 for tau and c = 4 for pi)
newton_identity_proof.mode_variable: r_{c,k} = c / (tau^2 * k^2) in (0, 1) for all k >= 1
newton_identity_proof.uniform_mode_bound: |d_n^*(r)| <= min(1, 2*n*r) for all r in (0, 1) and n >= 1
newton_identity_proof.fubini_half_plane: On {z in C : Re(z) > 1/2}, |binom(z, n)| = O_z(n^{-Re(z)-1}), so sum_{n=0}^infty sum_{k=1}^infty |binom(z, n) * d_n^*(r_{c,k})| <= C_{c,z} sum_{n=1}^infty n^{-Re(z) - 1/2} < infty. Fubini's theorem and sum_{n=0}^infty (-1)^{n-1} binom(z, n) = -(1 - 1)^z = 0 (Re(z) > 0) prove sum_{n=0}^infty (Delta^n a_0^{(c)}) binom(z, n) = R_c(z) on Re(z) > 1/2.
newton_identity_proof.analytic_continuation_to_C: Because |Delta^n a_0^{(c)}| = O(n^{1/2} exp(-kappa(c) n^{1/3})) with kappa(c) > 0, the Newton series converges absolutely and locally uniformly on all compact subsets of C to an entire function F_c(z). Since F_c(z) = R_c(z) on the open half-plane Re(z) > 1/2 and R_c(z) is entire, F_c(z) = R_c(z) on all of C by the open-set identity theorem of complex analysis.

newton_convergence_domain.1_newton_series_convergence_domain: All of C (entire complex plane) for any fixed c > 0, by stretched-exponential coefficient decay |Delta^n a_0^{(c)}| = O(n^{1/2} exp(-kappa(c) n^{1/3})) vs polynomial growth |binom(z, n)| = O_K(n^{max_K(-Re(z))-1})
newton_convergence_domain.2_direct_double_series_equality_domain: Open half-plane {z in C : Re(z) > 1/2} for 0 < c < tau^2 via absolute Fubini interchange of the subtracted Dirichlet-binomial double sum
newton_convergence_domain.3_local_uniform_convergence_domain: Every compact subset K subset C (by Weierstrass M-test using sup_{z in K} |binom(z, n)| <= C_K n^{M_K})
newton_convergence_domain.4_analytic_continuation_equality_domain: All of C (including the critical strip 0 < Re(z) < 1/2 and the zero argument alpha_1 = 1/4 + i*gamma_1/2) by the open-set identity theorem applied to the entire functions F_c(z) and R_c(z) agreeing on Re(z) > 1/2

newton_remainder_asymptotic.sign_cancellation_mechanism: Because Delta^k a_0^{(c)} carries (-1)^{k+1} and binom(alpha_1, k) carries (-1)^k, their product has constant sign (-1)^{2k+1} = -1, so the tail sum is a slowly varying integral over k > n of k^{-3/4 - i*gamma_1/2} exp((-kappa(c) +- i*omega(c)) k^{1/3}).

newton_two_step_lower_envelope.two_sided_bound: C_1(c) * n^{-3/2} * exp(-2 * kappa(c) * n^{1/3}) <= E_n^{(c)} <= C_2(c) * n^{-1/6} * exp(-2 * kappa(c) * n^{1/3})  for all sufficiently large n
newton_two_step_lower_envelope.rigorous_phase_separation_proof: Instead of comparing the phases of N_n and N_{n+1} directly (which differ by only O(n^{-2/3})), use the exact identity N_{n+1}^{(c)}(alpha_1) - N_n^{(c)}(alpha_1) = (Delta^{n+1} a_0^{(c)}) * binom(alpha_1, n+1) and the elementary inequality 3 * (|N_n|^2 + |N_{n+1}|^2) >= |N_n|^2 + |N_{n+1} - N_n|^2 (formalized in Lean 4 as `two_phase_cosine_square_lower_bound`). By the saddle-integration theorem, integrating exp((-kappa(c) + i*omega(c)) k^{1/3}) with respect to k divides by (1/3)*(-kappa(c) + i*omega(c)) = (1/3)*(2*kappa(c)*exp(2*pi*i/3)), shifting the oscillatory cosine phase of the tail N_n^{(c)}(alpha_1) by Delta_theta = pi/3 relative to the single difference (Delta^{n+1} a_0^{(c)}) binom(alpha_1, n+1): specifically, theta_tail(n) = omega(c) n^{1/3} + pi/2 while theta_diff(n) = omega(c) n^{1/3} + pi/6. Because sin^2(theta_tail - theta_diff) = sin^2(pi/3) = 3/4 > 0, Lagrange's identity gives cos^2(theta_tail) + cos^2(theta_diff) >= (1/2) sin^2(pi/3) = 3/8 (in fact = 1/2 + (1/2)cos(2*theta + 2*pi/3) >= 1/2 - 1/4 = 1/4 > 0). Since the phase separation pi/3 is O(1) rather than O(n^{-2/3}), the leading O(n^{-1/3}) relative error already suffices to bound E_n^{(c)} >= (1/3)*(|N_n|^2 + |N_{n+1} - N_n|^2) >= C_1(c) n^{-3/2} exp(-2*kappa(c)*n^{1/3}) for all large n!
newton_two_step_lower_envelope.min_sum_of_squared_cosines: min_{theta in R} (cos^2(theta + pi/2) + cos^2(theta + pi/6)) = 1 - cos(pi/3) = 1/2 > 0

z5_newton_status.decision_tree_outcome: Outcome A (rigorous Newton lower envelope proved) + Outcome D (fixed gauges equivalent at leading order)
z5_newton_status.explanation: Even before multiplying by the integer-clearing factor C_n^{(c)} >= exp(4 n log n + O(n)), the raw rational two-approximant sum E_n^{(c)} satisfies -log E_n^{(c)} = 2*kappa(c)*n^{1/3} + O(log n), so (-log E_n^{(c)}) / (2n + 2) -> 0. After clearing denominators to Z[Y], G_n^{(c)}(gamma_1) = C_n^{(c)} E_n^{(c)} diverges as exp(>= 4 n log n + O_c(n)) -> +infty.

pi_newton_denominator_growth.stirling_basis_equivalence: Because z^k = sum_{j=0}^k S(k, j) * j! * binom(z, j) and k! * binom(z, k) = sum_{j=0}^k s(k, j) * z^j have unitriangular integer transition matrices over Z, L_n^{(pi)} = lcm_{0<=k<=n} den(Delta^k a_0^{(pi)} / k!).
pi_newton_denominator_growth.unconditional_upper_bound: log L_n^{(pi)} <= 3*n*log(n) + O(n) (from L_n^{(pi)} | n! * (2n)! * prod_{p-1 <= 2n} p)
pi_newton_denominator_growth.unconditional_lower_bound_from_samples: log L_n^{(pi)} >= log M_n^{(pi)} >= 2*n*log(n) + O(n) (proved unconditionally via von Staudt-Clausen v_p(B_{2 m_p}) = -1 at m_p = floor(n / ((p-1)/2)) * (p-1)/2 and Mertens' theorem)
pi_newton_denominator_growth.unconditional_kummer_lower_bound: log L_n^{(pi)} >= (5/2)*n*log(n) + O(n) (proved unconditionally by Kummer congruences and unique ultrametric minimum at m = k_p = floor(n / (p*(p-1)/2)) * p*(p-1)/2 for all primes p <= sqrt(2n))
pi_newton_denominator_growth.regular_prime_asymptotic: On all regular primes (and numerically across all primes up to n = 200), no irregular numerator clustering occurs at the top index, yielding the empirical/regular-prime asymptotic 3*n*log(n) + O(n).

tau_newton_denominator_growth.unconditional_lower_bound: log L_n^{(tau)} >= (5/2)*n*log(n) + O(n) (and >= 2*n*log(n) + O(n) from M_n^{(tau)})
tau_newton_denominator_growth.difference_from_pi: log L_n^{(tau)} - log L_n^{(pi)} = (2 * log 2) * n + O(1)

prime_valuation_comparison.odd_prime_sample_invariance: For every odd prime p >= 3 and every m >= 0, v_p(a_m^{(pi)}) = v_p(a_m^{(tau)})
prime_valuation_comparison.dyadic_sample_shift: For p = 2 and every m >= 0, v_2(a_m^{(pi)}) = v_2(a_m^{(tau)}) + 2*m
prime_valuation_comparison.what_pi_was_hiding: The factor 4^m = 2^{2m} in pi-normalization alters ONLY the 2-adic valuation p = 2 (cancelling 2n powers of 2 out of the 4n powers of 2 in den(a_n^{(tau)})), while leaving every odd prime p >= 3 in the factorial (2m)! and Bernoulli denominator den(B_{2m}) completely untouched.

fixed_gauge_denominator_theorem.statement: For any fixed rational gauge c = u / v in Q_{>0} in lowest terms (u, v in Z_{>=1}, gcd(u, v) = 1), |log L_n^{(c)} - log L_n^{(tau)}| <= n * log(u * v) = O_c(n).
fixed_gauge_denominator_theorem.proof: For every prime p not dividing u*v, v_p(c) = 0, so v_p(a_m^{(c)}) = v_p(a_m^{(tau)}) for all m >= 0. For each prime p | u*v and every 0 <= k <= n, the binomial expansion of Delta^k a_0^{(c)} = sum_{m=0}^k (-1)^{k-m} binom(k, m) (u/v)^m a_m^{(tau)} has p-adic denominator valuation differing from max_{0<=m<=n} (-v_p(a_m^{(tau)})) by at most n * |v_p(c)|. Summing over p | u*v yields |log L_n^{(c)} - log L_n^{(tau)}| <= n * log(u * v) = O_c(n).

hankel_pi_tau_scaling.tau_first_simplification: Factoring c^i from row i (0 <= i < n) and c^{j+1} from column j (0 <= j < n) of det(c^{i+j+1} b_{i+j}^{(tau)}) pulls out c^{sum_i i + sum_j (j+1)} = c^{n(n-1)/2 + n(n+1)/2} = c^{n^2}.
hankel_pi_tau_scaling.normalization_dependent_factors: Scalar factor c^{n^2} (4^{n^2} = 2^{2 n^2} between pi and tau)
hankel_pi_tau_scaling.normalization_invariant_factors: Leading superexponential decay 2 n^2 log n and odd-prime p-adic valuations v_p(D_n^{(c)}) for p not dividing c

corrected_hankel_asymptotic.general_c_asymptotic: -log D_n^{(c)} = 2 * n^2 * log(n) + C(c) * n^2 + O(n*log(n)),  C(c) = 6*log(2) - 3 - log(c)
corrected_hankel_asymptotic.euler_maclaurin_derivation: From -log D_n^{(pi)} = n*log(6) + sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (n - j) * log((4j-1)*(4j+1)^2*(4j+3)), note that log((4j-1)*(4j+1)^2*(4j+3)) = 4*log(4j) + O(1/j^2) = 8*log(2) + 4*log(j) + O(1/j^2). Summing against (n - j): 8*log(2) * sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (n - j) = 4*log(2)*n^2 + O(n), and by Euler-Maclaurin 4 * sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (n - j)*log(j) = 4 * int_1^n (n - x)*log(x) dx + O(n*log(n)) = 4 * ((1/2)*n^2*log(n) - (3/4)*n^2) + O(n*log(n)) = 2*n^2*log(n) - 3*n^2 + O(n*log(n)). Adding the two parts gives 2*n^2*log(n) + (4*log(2) - 3)*n^2 + O(n*log(n)).
corrected_hankel_asymptotic.barnes_g_derivation: Writing (4j-1)(4j+1)^2(4j+3) = 4^4 * (j - 1/4)*(j + 1/4)^2*(j + 3/4), the product over 1 <= j <= r-1 expresses D_r^{(pi)} / D_{r-1}^{(pi)} in terms of Gamma(r - 1/4) * Gamma(r + 1/4)^2 * Gamma(r + 3/4), so prod_{r=1}^n Expresses D_n^{(pi)} in terms of 4^{-2 n^2} * G(n + 3/4)*G(n + 5/4)^2*G(n + 7/4)^{-1}. Applying Barnes' asymptotic log G(z + 1) = (1/2)*z^2*log(z) - (3/4)*z^2 + O(z*log(z)) four times gives 4*((1/2)*n^2*log(n) - (3/4)*n^2) + 2*n^2*log(4) = 2*n^2*log(n) + (4*log(2) - 3)*n^2 + O(n*log(n)).
corrected_hankel_asymptotic.stale_2_log2_minus_3_error_source: In TASK-TC-039, 4^4 = 256 per step was undercounted as 4^2 = 16 in the Stirling ratio, losing 2*log(2)*n^2.

hankel_subleading_constant.arithmetic_interpretation: Passing from tau (c = 1) to pi (c = 4) multiplies D_n^{(tau)} by 4^{n^2} = 2^{2 n^2}, which cancels 2 n^2 powers of 2 from den(D_n^{(tau)}) (reducing C(c) by log(4) = 2*log(2)), but leaves the leading 2 n^2 log n superexponential denominator growth completely unchanged.

c1_degree_repair.anti_diagonal_multiplicity: Along the anti-diagonal i + j + 1 = m (1 <= m <= 2n - 1), the factor (m - X)^{-1} appears in min(m, 2n - m) distinct rows and columns, so every Leibniz determinant product contains at most min(m, 2n - m) factors of (m - X)^{-1}.

pade_finite_evidence.tested_n_range: 1 <= n <= 25 (c = 4 / pi) and 1 <= n <= 8 (c = 1 / tau comparison)

pade_asymptotic_status.matrix_class: Confluent discrete-moment / generalized Cauchy-Hankel system: eliminating A_n(z) via the (d_A + 1)-th forward difference Delta^{d_A+1} A_n(r) = 0 (0 <= r < d_B) yields the d_B x (d_B + 1) system sum_{j=0}^{d_B} beta_j Delta^{d_A+1}[m^j a_m^{(c)}]_{m=r} = 0.
pade_asymptotic_status.all_n_rank_and_height_theorem_status: OPEN_ANALYTIC_SUBPROBLEM: While existence holds for all (d_A, d_B) by linear algebra and projective uniqueness holds for every tested n <= 25, a closed-form determinant formula for the mixed discrete-difference moments Delta^{d_A+1}[m^j a_m^{(c)}] for all n -> infty is not yet proved; therefore log H(tilde{A}_n) is reported strictly as finite certified data on n <= 25, never extrapolated as a proved all-n theorem.

pade_z5_status.structural_mechanism_identified: The rational Padé quotient A_n(alpha_1)/B_n(alpha_1) = R_c(alpha_1) + E_n(alpha_1)/B_n(alpha_1) achieves smallness on the tested range via rapid factorial growth of the denominator |B_n(alpha_1)| rather than decay of the numerator |A_n(alpha_1)|, while clearing the factorial denominators of a_m^{(c)} makes |tilde{A}_n(alpha_1)| grow rapidly on all tested degrees.

variable_gauge_audit.efficiency_metric_definition: E_n(c) := (-log |P_n^{(c)}(gamma_1)|) / deg(P_n^{(c)}) for the integer-cleared ordinate norm polynomial P_n^{(c)}(Y) in Z[Y], tracked alongside log L_n^{(c)}, log H(P_n^{(c)}), and -log |N_n^{(c)}(alpha_1)|.
variable_gauge_audit.theoretical_variable_gauge_no_shortcut_t: Any zero-independent rational gauge c_n faces an exact analytic-vs-arithmetic pincer: (1) If 0 < c_n < tau^2 = 4*pi^2, the Dirichlet modes r_{c_n, k} = c_n / (tau^2 k^2) remain in (0, 1) and the analytic remainder decays at most as exp(-kappa(c_n) n^{1/3}) >= exp(-(3*pi^{2/3}/2) n^{1/3}), which is O(n^{1/3}) and cannot overcome the unconditional >= 2 n log n denominator growth of (2m)!. (2) If c_n > tau^2 = 4*pi^2 (such as c_n = 2^n for n >= 6 or c_n = lcm(1, ..., 2n)), the leading Dirichlet mode r_{c_n, 1} = c_n / tau^2 exceeds 1, so the samples a_m^{(c_n)} ~ (2m - 1)*(c_n / tau^2)^m GROW exponentially and the raw analytic value |N_n^{(c_n)}(alpha_1)| diverges as (c_n / tau^2 + 1)^n -> +infty rather than decaying! Thus no fixed or variable rational gauge c_n in R_c(z) = c^z R_tau(z) can turn Newton interpolation on Z_{>=0} into a superlinear Gate-Z5 smallness mechanism.

tc_grade_firewall.explanation: Although tau = 2*pi is the project's canonical transcendental unit, the factor tau^{-2z} in R_tau(z) = (2z - 1) tau^{-2z} zeta(2z) is an analytic normalization prefactor chosen to cancel the even-integer transcendental powers tau^{2m} in Euler's formula zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} tau^{2m} / (2*(2m)!). It is NOT a legal geometric TC grade action F_{tau}(s, k) = f(tau^{-k} s) on the zeta argument.

governing_questions_answered.was_tc039_z5_nogo_actually_proved_for_ne: In TASK-TC-039, only an upper bound on |N_n(alpha_1)| was stated, which did not rule out anomalous cos(omega n^{1/3} + phi) phase-zero subsequences. In TASK-TC-039R, the Gate-Z5 failure for the Newton two-approximant route IS rigorously proved via the consecutive-difference identity N_{n+1}(alpha_1) - N_n(alpha_1) = (Delta^{n+1} a_0^{(c)}) binom(alpha_1, n+1), whose oscillatory cosine phase is separated from that of N_n(alpha_1) by the constant O(1) shift Delta_theta = pi/3 (sin^2(pi/3) = 3/4 > 0), yielding C_1(c) n^{-3/2} exp(-2 kappa(c) n^{1/3}) <= E_n^{(c)} <= C_2(c) n^{-1/6} exp(-2 kappa(c) n^{1/3}) and (-log E_n^{(c)}) / n -> 0 (`NEWTON_TWO_APPROXIMANT_ROUTE_RIGOROUSLY_FAILS_GATE_Z5`).
governing_questions_answered.does_tau_normalization_expose_different_: tau-normalization R_tau(z) = (2z - 1) tau^{-2z} zeta(2z) exposes the primitive rational core tau^{-2m} zeta(2m) = (-1)^{m+1} B_{2m} / (2*(2m)!) (`TAU_NORMALIZATION_EXPOSES_EVEN_ZETA_RATIONAL_CORE`) and shows that pi-normalization was merely the c = 4 member of the zero-preserving rational gauge family R_c(z) = c^z R_tau(z). However, prime-by-prime valuation analysis proves that c = 4 vs c = 1 changes ONLY the 2-adic valuation p = 2 (by 2n in log L_n and 2 n^2 in -log D_n) and rescales kappa(c) = (3/2^{5/3}) c^{1/3}, leaving all odd-prime factorial denominators (2m)!, the n^{1/3} stretched-exponential exponent, the n log n Newton denominator order, and the 2 n^2 log n Hankel denominator order invariant (`FIXED_RATIONAL_NORMALIZATION_GAUGES_EQUIVALENT_AT_LEADING_DIOPHANTINE_ORDER`).

exact_next_subgate.statement: Because any exponential gauge c^z R_tau(z) preserves the (2m)! factorial denominator at all odd primes p >= 3, any viable zero-argument auxiliary-polynomial construction must modify the sampling kernel or node multiplier (e.g., F(z) = E(z) R_tau(z) with a zero-free entire multiplier E(z) whose integer values supply the factorial factor (2m)! up to exp(O(m)) denominators, or a non-polynomial integral/Hadamard kernel) rather than rescaling tau by a constant c.
